prompt: Some people believe that the increasing use of computers and mobile phones for communications has had a negative effect on young people's reading and writing skills. > To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Nowadays, many people believe that the increasing use of phones and computers is harmful to children’s knowledge and literacy skills. I completely agree with this view.

On the one hand, modern technology is developing rapidly, and children can acquire a wide range of skills through digital devices such as mobile phones and computers. For instance, in the past, children typically wrote essays by hand, whereas nowadays they often use keyboards, meaning that they have to develop typing skills while completing their written tasks. Moreover, the increasing use of digital devices can have a positive effect on teenagers’ writing abilities, since some software enables them to identify and correct their mistakes rather than repeatedly making the same errors.

On the other hand, excessive use of these technologies can undermine children’s reading and writing abilities. This is because young people tend to spend a considerable amount of time consuming digital content, such as social-media posts and short messages, rather than reading lengthy and well-structured texts. As a result, they may experience difficulties in understanding complex information. Furthermore, children may gradually lose their spelling skills because they become overly dependent on autocorrect when writing. Consequently, they may develop poor spelling habits without even being aware of their mistakes.

In conclusion, although the increasing use of computers and mobile phones can provide children with valuable opportunities to develop their writing skills, excessive reliance on these technologies may negatively affect their reading ability and spelling. Therefore, I partly agree that the growing use of digital devices has had a detrimental effect on young people’s literacy skills.
